speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. You are presenting with a rash on your scalp and forehead; can you describe when this first appeared and if you have noticed any blisters, crusting, or oozing?

speaker: Patient
text: 3-month-old boy. The parents report that the rash has been present for several weeks, noting that it sometimes appears red and scaly, especially during cold weather. The patient was born at 36 weeks' gestation and has been generally healthy since. The patient's father has a history of psoriasis.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that history. Given his age, the worsening in cold weather, and his family history, this could be psoriasis or eczema; has the rash appeared in any other areas like the elbows, knees, or behind his ears? Also, has he been tested for eczema or psoriasis before?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Rash on scalp and forehead. I also have Erythematous patches, Greasy yellow scales, Worse in cold weather.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Cradle Cap (Infantile Seborrheic Dermatitis)

The presence of greasy yellow scales on the scalp and forehead, worsening in cold weather, combined with a family history of psoriasis, strongly supports this diagnosis. Would you like me to request any images of the rash to confirm the findings?
